verses.zh: 亚当生塞特；塞特生以挪士；
verses.en: Adam, Seth, Enosh,

verses.zh: 以挪士生该南；该南生玛勒列；玛勒列生雅列；
verses.en: Kenan, Mahalalel, Jered,

verses.zh: 雅列生以诺；以诺生玛土撒拉；玛土撒拉生拉麦；
verses.en: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

verses.zh: 拉麦生挪亚；挪亚生闪、含、雅弗。
verses.en: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Shem, Ham, and Japheth were Noah’s three sons (Gen 6:10).tc The LXX reads “Noah; the sons of Noah [were] Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Several English translations (e.g., NIV, NLT) follow the LXX.

verses.zh: 雅弗的儿子是歌篾、玛各、玛代、雅完、土巴、米设、提拉。
verses.en: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

verses.zh: 歌篾的儿子是亚实基拿、低法（在创世记十章三节是利法）、陀迦玛。
verses.en: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath,[NOTE:1] and Togarmah.
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss, along with the LXX and Vulgate, read “Riphath” (see Gen 10:3). This is followed by several English translations (e.g., NAB, NIV, NLT), while others (e.g., ASV, NASB, NRSV) follow the MT reading (“Diphath”).

verses.zh: 雅完的儿子是以利沙、他施、基提、多单。
verses.en: The sons[NOTE:1] of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or in this case, “descendants.”

Heb “Kittim and Rodanim.”tc The Kethib has רוֹדָנִים (Rodanim), which probably refers to the island of Rhodes. The Qere has דּוֹדָנִים (Dodanim), which refers to one of the most ancient and revered locations in ancient Greece. The MT and most medieval Hebrew mss of the parallel list in Gen 10:4 read “Dodanim,” but a few have “Rodanim.”

verses.zh: 含的儿子是古实、麦西、弗、迦南。
verses.en: The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim,[NOTE:1] Put, and Canaan.
notes: That is, “Egypt.”

verses.zh: 古实的儿子是西巴、哈腓拉、撒弗他、拉玛、撒弗提迦。拉玛的儿子是示巴、底但。
verses.en: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca.The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

verses.zh: 古实生宁录；他为世上英雄之首。
verses.en: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who established himself as a mighty warrior on earth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he began to be a mighty warrior in the earth.”

verses.zh: 麦西生路低人、亚拿米人、利哈比人、拿弗土希人、
verses.en: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

verses.zh: 帕斯鲁细人、迦斯路希人、迦斐托人；从迦斐托出来的有非利士人。
verses.en: Pathrusites, Casluhites (from whom the Philistines descended[NOTE:1]) , and the Caphtorites.
notes: Heb “came forth.”

verses.zh: 迦南生长子西顿，又生赫
verses.en: Canaan was the father of Sidon—his firstborn—and Heth,

verses.zh: 和耶布斯人、亚摩利人、革迦撒人、
verses.en: as well as the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites,

verses.zh: 希未人、亚基人、西尼人、
verses.en: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,

verses.zh: 亚瓦底人、洗玛利人，并哈马人。
verses.en: Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.

verses.zh: 闪的儿子是以拦、亚述、亚法撒、路德、亚兰、乌斯、户勒、基帖、米设（在创世记十章二十三节是玛施）。
verses.en: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.The sons of Aram:[NOTE:1] Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “the sons of Aram” do not appear in the Hebrew text. Apparently the phrase וּבְנֵי אֲרָם (uvene ʾaram) has accidentally dropped out of the text by homoioteleuton (note the presence of אֲרָם just before this). The phrase is included in Gen 10:23.
The MT of the parallel geneaology in Gen 10:23 reads “Mash,” but the LXX there reads “Meshech” in agreement with 1 Chr 1:17.

verses.zh: 亚法撒生沙拉；沙拉生希伯。
verses.en: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.

verses.zh: 希伯生了两个儿子：一个名叫法勒（就是分的意思），因为那时人就分地居住；法勒的兄弟名叫约坍。
verses.en: Two sons were born to Eber: the first was named Peleg, for during his lifetime the earth was divided;[NOTE:1] his brother’s name was Joktan.
notes: Perhaps this refers to the scattering of the people at Babel (Gen 11:1-9).

verses.zh: 约坍生亚摩答、沙列、哈萨玛非、耶拉、
verses.en: Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

verses.zh: 哈多兰、乌萨、德拉、
verses.en: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

verses.zh: 以巴录、亚比玛利、示巴、
verses.en: Ebal,[NOTE:1] Abimael, Sheba,
notes: Some medieval Hebrew mss and the Syriac read “Obal” (see Gen 10:28).

verses.zh: 阿斐、哈腓拉、约巴。这都是约坍的儿子。
verses.en: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

verses.zh: 闪生亚法撒；亚法撒生沙拉；
verses.en: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,[NOTE:1]
notes: Some LXX mss read “Arphaxad, Cainan, Shelah” (see also the notes on Gen 10:24; 11:12-13).

verses.zh: 沙拉生希伯；希伯生法勒；法勒生拉吴；
verses.en: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

verses.zh: 拉吴生西鹿；西鹿生拿鹤；拿鹤生他拉；
verses.en: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

verses.zh: 他拉生亚伯兰，亚伯兰就是亚伯拉罕。
verses.en: Abram (that is, Abraham).

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕的儿子是以撒、以实玛利。
verses.en: The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

verses.zh: 以实玛利的儿子记在下面：以实玛利的长子是尼拜约，其次是基达、押德别、米比衫、
verses.en: These were their descendants:Ishmael’s firstborn son was Nebaioth; the others were[NOTE:1] Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
notes: The words “the others were” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 米施玛、度玛、玛撒、哈达、提玛、
verses.en: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,

verses.zh: 伊突、拿非施、基底玛。这都是以实玛利的儿子。
verses.en: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕的妾基土拉所生的儿子，就是心兰、约珊、米但、米甸、伊施巴、书亚。约珊的儿子是示巴、底但。
verses.en: The sons to whom Keturah, Abraham’s concubine,[NOTE:1] gave birth: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah.The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
notes: A concubine was a slave woman in ancient Near Eastern societies who was the legal property of her master, but who could have legitimate sexual relations with her master. A concubine’s status was more elevated than a mere servant, but she was not free and did not have the legal rights of a free wife. The children of a concubine could, in some instances, become equal heirs with the children of the free wife. After the period of the Judges concubines may have become more of a royal prerogative (2 Sam 21:10-14; 1 Kgs 11:3).

verses.zh: 米甸的儿子是以法、以弗、哈诺、亚比大、以勒大。这都是基土拉的子孙。
verses.en: The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕生以撒；以撒的儿子是以扫和以色列。
verses.en: Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.

verses.zh: 以扫的儿子是以利法、流珥、耶乌施、雅兰、可拉。
verses.en: The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

verses.zh: 以利法的儿子是提幔、阿抹、洗玻、迦坦、基纳斯、亭纳、亚玛力。
verses.en: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi,[NOTE:1] Gatam, Kenaz, and (by Timna) Amalek.[NOTE:2]
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss, along with some LXX mss and the Syriac, read “Zepho” (see Gen 36:11).

The Hebrew text has simply, “and Timna and Amalek,” but Gen 36:12 indicates that Timna, a concubine of Eliphaz, was the mother of Amalek. See also v. 39 below, which states that Timna was the sister of Lotan.

verses.zh: 流珥的儿子是拿哈、谢拉、沙玛、米撒。
verses.en: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

verses.zh: 西珥的儿子是罗坍、朔巴、祭便、亚拿、底顺、以察、底珊。
verses.en: The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

verses.zh: 罗坍的儿子是何利、荷幔；罗坍的妹子是亭纳。
verses.en: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. (Timna was Lotan’s sister.)[NOTE:1]
notes: Perhaps this is the Timna mentioned in v. 36.

verses.zh: 朔巴的儿子是亚勒文、玛拿辖、以巴录、示非、阿南。祭便的儿子是亚雅、亚拿。
verses.en: The sons of Shobal: Alyan,[NOTE:1] Manahath, Ebal, Shephi,[NOTE:2] and Onam.The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
notes: Some medieval Hebrew mss and a few LXX mss read “Alvan” (see Gen 36:23).
A few medieval Hebrew mss read “Shepho” (see Gen 36:23).

verses.zh: 亚拿的儿子是底顺。底顺的儿子是哈默兰、伊是班、益兰、基兰。
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Anah: Dishon.The sons of Dishon: Hamran,[NOTE:2] Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.
notes: Heb “sons.” The Hebrew text has the plural, but only one son is listed. For stylistic reasons the singular “son” was used in the translation.
The parallel geneaology in Gen 36:26 has the variant spelling “Hemdan.” Some English versions follow the variant spelling here (e.g., NAB, NIV, NCV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 以察的儿子是辟罕、撒番、亚干。底珊的儿子是乌斯、亚兰。
verses.en: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, Jaakan.[NOTE:1] The sons of Dishan:[NOTE:2] Uz and Aran.
notes: The parallel geneaology in Gen 36:27 has the variant spelling “Akan.” Among English versions that use the variant spelling here are NIV, NCV, NLT.
The MT reads “Dishon” here, but this should be emended to “Dishan.” See the list in v. 38 and Gen 36:28.

verses.zh: 以色列人未有君王治理之先，在以东地作王的记在下面：有比珥的儿子比拉，他的京城名叫亭哈巴。
verses.en: These were the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king ruled over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor; the name of his city was Dinhabah.

verses.zh: 比拉死了，波斯拉人谢拉的儿子约巴接续他作王。
verses.en: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “ruled in his place,” here and in vv. 45-50.

verses.zh: 约巴死了，提幔地的人户珊接续他作王。
verses.en: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him.

verses.zh: 户珊死了，比达的儿子哈达接续他作王。这哈达就是在摩押地杀败米甸人的，他的京城名叫亚未得。
verses.en: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad succeeded him. He struck down the Midianites in the plains of Moab; the name of his city was Avith.

verses.zh: 哈达死了，玛士利加人桑拉接续他作王。
verses.en: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him.

verses.zh: 桑拉死了，大河边的利河伯人扫罗接续他作王。
verses.en: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the River[NOTE:1] succeeded him.
notes: Or “near the river.” sn The river may refer to the Euphrates River (cf. NRSV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 扫罗死了，亚革波的儿子巴勒・哈南接续他作王。
verses.en: When Shaul died, Baal Hanan son of Achbor succeeded him.

verses.zh: 巴勒・哈南死了，哈达接续他作王。他的京城名叫巴伊，他的妻子名叫米希她别，是米・萨合的孙女，玛特列的女儿。
verses.en: When Baal Hanan died, Hadad succeeded him; the name of his city was Pai.[NOTE:1] His wife[NOTE:2] was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-Zahab.
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss, along with some LXX mss, the Syriac, and Vulgate, read “Pau.” See also Gen 36:39.
Heb “The name of his wife.”

verses.zh: 哈达死了，以东人的族长有亭纳族长、亚勒瓦族长、耶帖族长、
verses.en: Hadad died.Tribal Chiefs of EdomThe tribal chiefs of Edom were: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

verses.zh: 亚何利巴玛族长、以拉族长、比嫩族长、
verses.en: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

verses.zh: 基纳斯族长、提幔族长、米比萨族长、
verses.en: Kenaz, Teman,[NOTE:1] Mibzar,
notes: Each of the names in this list is preceded by the word “chief” in the Hebrew text. This has not been included in the translation because it would appear very redundant to the modern reader.

verses.zh: 玛基叠族长、以兰族长。这都是以东人的族长。
verses.en: Magdiel, and Iram.[NOTE:1] These were the tribal chiefs of Edom.

* Although they are not inspired, paragraph divisions are the key to understanding and following the original
author's intent. Each modern translation has divided and summarized the paragraphs. Every paragraph has one central topic, truth, or
thought. Each version encapsulates that topic in its own distinct way. As you read the text, ask yourself which translation fits your
understanding of the subject and verse divisions.

In every chapter we must read the Bible first and try to identify its subjects (paragraphs), then compare our
understanding with the modern versions. Only when we understand the original author's intent by following his logic and presentation
can we truly understand the Bible. Only the original author is inspired - readers have no right to change or modify the message.
Bible readers do have the responsibility of applying the inspired truth to their day and their lives.

Note that all technical terms and abbreviations are explained fully in the following documents:
Hebrew Grammatical Tems,
Textual Criticism,
and Glossary.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Chronicles starts with Adam not Abraham. There is an eternal purpose in creation as well as an eternal
redemptive plan.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL
REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- Note the progression.

- Adam (Cain and Abel not mentioned) to Noah, 1 Chr. 1:1-4

- Noah's children, 1 Chr. 1:4,5-23

- Shem, 1 Chr. 1:17-23 (emphasis noted by length of genealogy)

- Ham, 1 Chr. 1:8-16

- Japheth, 1 Chr. 1:5-7

- Shem to Abraham, 1 Chr. 1:24-27

- descendants of Abraham, 1 Chr. 1:28-42

- Ishmael, 1 Chr. 1:29-33

- Isaac, 1 Chr. 1:35-42

(1) Esau, 1 Chr. 1:35-42

(2) Israel/Jacob (picks up in second chapter)

- leaders in Esau's family, 1 Chr. 1:43-54

SPECIAL
TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

- A Hebrew post-exilic hearer/reader would immediately relate to the book of Genesis. Many of these names had special
meaning to the Jewish people. Their story as a people is reflected in this text!

- Often these individual's names later referred to

- families

- tribes

- regions

- nations

- towns

- languages (i.e., Genesis 10-11)

For a good brief discussion of the sub-genre of genealogies see NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 654-662.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1:1-7

1Adam, Seth, Enosh, 2Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, 3Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
4Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. 5The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan,
Tubal, Meshech and Tiras. 6The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
7The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Rodanim.

1:1 "Adam" This Hebrew word (BDB 9; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 262-266) is the general term for human person.

- a man ‒ Gen. 2:5,7,8,15,16,18,19

- mankind ‒ Gen. 1:26; 6:2,5,6,7; 9:5,6

- both male and female ‒ Gen. 1:27; 5:2

- proper name ‒ possibly Gen. 2:19,20,21,23; 3:8,9,17,20,21; 4:1,25; 5:1,2,3,4,5; Deut. 32:8; 1 Chr. 1:1

It is often hard, in the context of Genesis, to know if God is addressing "the man" or Adam.

▣ "Enosh" He is mentioned in Gen. 4:26; 5:6,7,9,10,11; 1 Chr. 1:1. His name (BDB 60) means "man" or
"mankind." It is used synonymously with "Adam" (BDB 9, see note at Gen. 2:20) in Job 25:6; Ps. 8:4; 96:3; 144:3;
Isa. 51:12; 56:2.

1:2 "Kenan" See Gen. 5:9-10 online. The meaning of his name is uncertain (BDB 884).

▣ "Mahalalel" See Gen. 5:13,15-17 online.

▣ "Jared" See Gen. 5:15 online.

1:3 "Enoch" See Gen. 5:18-24 online. He (BDB 335) was taken to be with God, Gen. 5:22-24.

▣ "Methuselah" See Gen. 5:25-27 online. He (BDB 607) lived longer than any person recorded in the OT.

▣ "Lamech" See Gen. 5:26-31 online. The person by this name (BDB 541) in Seth's line is hopeful of
God's mercy, while the one by the same name in Cain's line is a violent man.

1:4 "Noah" See Gen. 5:29 online. The sons of this "blameless" man (cf. Gen. 6:9) are named in Gen. 5:32.

His life is recorded in Genesis 6-9.

His sons' genealogies are recorded in Genesis 10.

- Japheth ‒ Gen. 10:2-5

- Ham ‒ Gen. 10:6-14,15-20

- Shem ‒ Gen. 10:21-31

1:5 These men and their descendants settled in modern Anatolia (Turkey) and are used as symbols of
rebellious nations in Ezekiel 38-39.

1:6 "Diphath" In Gen. 10:3, "Riphath" (LXX). The Hebrew letters "d" and "r" are very similar and often
confused in Hebrew writings.

1:7 "Rodanim" In Gen. 10:4 it is "Dodanim" (LXX). Again, a confusion of the "d" and "r."

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1:8-10

8The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. 9The sons of Cush
were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
10Cush became the father of Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one in the earth.

1:8 "Canaan" His children are mentioned in 1 Chr. 1:13-16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

1:9 "Raamah" Sometimes the name has the final "h" (cf. Gen. 10:7) and sometimes not (MT of 1 Chr. 1:9).

Both names appear in 1 Chr. 1:9.

1:10 "Nimrod" See Gen. 10:8,9 online. He (BDB 650) was a mighty man whose life is described in Genesis 10;
see notes there.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1:11-12

11Mizraim became the father of the people of Lud, Anam, Lehab, Naphtuh, 12Pathrus, Casluh,
from which the Philistines came, and Caphtor.

1:11 "Mizraim" See Gen. 10:13 online. He (BDB 595) and his descendants would become the inhabitants
of southern Egypt.

1:12 "from which the Philistines came" This phrase relates to "Caphtor" (cf. Amos 9:7) not "Casluh" (i.e.,
1 Chr. 1:12). For notes on the Philistines see Gen. 26:1 online.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1:13-16

13Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, Heth, 14and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the
Girgashites, 15the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites, 16the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the purpose(s) of the extended genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1-9?

- Which OT covenant does Chronicles seem to elevate and why?

- Why is 1 Chronicles different from Samuel?

- Why does this genealogy start with Adam and not Abraham?

- If this is a genealogy of the people of God, Israel, why such a long list of Edomite leaders?
